messages:
claire (PM): Quick sync — proposing a new multi-quarter initiative: Regional Policy & Isolation runway. Goal: clear routing primitives + SLA tiers so sales can promise region-bounded SLAs. Need input on prioritization, launch criteria, and major risks. TL;DR: customers keep asking for stronger isolation guarantees and predictable cross-region failover.

sumit (Arch): +1. We should separate policy primitives (affinity, fallback, quarantine) from enforcement surfaces. That lets us ship lightweight policy DSL first, then binding to infra.

diego (Eng): Agree. From implementation POV, two big efforts: runtime routing engine (low-latency decisioning) and infra changes for tenant-slices. ETA for a minimal prototype ~8w if we scope to single-region policy + synthetic traffic tests.

anya (SRE): Ops concerns: need observability hooks per-route (p95 latency, drop/reject counts, eviction events). Also want rollback story for policy flips — automated fallback to global default.

michael (Sales): Customer asks: 1) geography pinning + data residency 2) SLA windows (99.9 regional) 3) isolation during noisy-neighbor events. Several mid-market deals contingent on this. We need clear launch language.

claire (PM): Proposed launch criteria (draft): a) policy DSL v1 documented + UI, b) runtime can route and fallback with <10ms decision latency at 95th, c) can declare region-bound SLAs with telemetry proving compliance for 2 weeks, d) disaster quiesce playbook. Thoughts?

sumit (Arch): Criteria make sense. Suggest we add gating: backward-compat rollout (policy defaults for existing customers) and a migration plan for pinned customers.

diego (Eng): Implementation detail: decision latency target depends on cache strategy. With local prefix cache we can hit <5ms, but cold path to policy store will spike. Need KV cache invalidation rules. Example DSL prototype: 
```
route {
  match: tenant == "T-123" && region == "eu-west-1"
  action: route_to(slice:europe-primary) fallback:slice:eu-fallback
  ttl: 30s
}
```

anya (SRE): Also recommend chaos tests: region failover, burst isolation, and policy API throttling. Add SLOs: policy propagation < 60s for 95%.

michael (Sales): Can we prioritize a quick win: per-tenant regional pinning + SLA docs first? Sales can use that in negotiations before full slice isolation ships.

claire (PM): Good call. Proposed phased launch: Phase 0 (docs + DSL + opt-in per-tenant pinning), Phase 1 (runtime routing + fallback + metrics), Phase 2 (tenant slices + reserved capacity + enforcement). Schedule draft: P0 in 4w, P1 in 12w, P2 in 24–36w.

sumit (Arch): We should call out risks: cross-region bandwidth egress costs, stateful caches consistency, and legal/data residency edge-cases. Add dependency on billing for egress visibility.

diego (Eng): Dependency note: infra team needs capacity tagging for slices. If sales routes customers into reserved pools, autoscaling rules must be different.

anya (SRE): Ops runbook stub: how to escalate when a slice is overloaded -> manual evac -> automated fallback. I'll drop a runbook PR.

claire (PM): Action items: Sumit write DSL spec (this week), Diego estimate runtime effort with infra (by EOD Fri), Anya start runbook PR, Michael collect top-3 customer commitments. I'll assemble these into a roadmap doc for exec review.

deploy-bot: deploy starting: infra/prototyping/policy-dsl -> staging at 1818225600 — check CI.

michael (Sales): One more ask — include a short customer-facing FAQ around "what happens during regional failover". Sales needs that for legal.

claire (PM): Noted. I'll add FAQ to P0 deliverables. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
